title: Mary E. Lovely on what's really going on with global supply chains
content_preview: How have US tariffs affected global supply chains? Are trading patterns between countries really changing? What can we learn from the fine print of trade agreements? Are the US and China really decoupling? PIIE Anthony M. Solomon Senior Fellow Mary E. Lovely dives into these questions and more with host Anjali V. Bhatt in this episode, exploring Lovely's recent research on global supply chains and US "reciprocal" trade agreements. cn_title: 玛丽·E·洛弗利：全球供应链的真实现状
cn_summary: 在本期节目中，PIIE高级研究员玛丽·E·洛弗利与主持人探讨美国关税对全球供应链的实际影响。她指出，尽管美国实施了多轮关税，但供应链的基本格局并未根本改变，企业仍在寻找成本最优的生产基地。洛弗利强调，贸易协定的细则往往决定了关税的实际执行力度，且美中“脱钩”更多是政治表态，经济层面仍保持高度互依。她的研究还揭示了过去关税政策对企业投资决策的长期影响。
impact: 关税波动可能导致中国制造业成本上升，推动企业加速向东南亚转移，但中国在高端制造和供应链控制方面仍具优势；对就业而言，若出口受阻，相关制造业岗位可能受压，青年毕业生面临更大竞争；宏观上，需加强内需和产业链自主可控，降低外部贸易摩擦风险。

title: Solar Has Crossed a Critical Economic Tipping Point
content_preview: For years, the economic case for solar came with an awkward qualification. Yes, it had no fuel bill. Yes, its operating costs were low. And yes, over the life of a project it could already produce cheaper electricity than a new coal or gas plant. But first, someone had to pay for it. Solar concentrated most of its lifetime costs at the beginning. Fossil power appeared to ask for less capital upfront and spread the rest of the bill across decades of coal or gas purchases. In rich countries with deep capital markets, that distinction could be managed.…
